name: Flint and steel
summary: A hard stone edge shaving burning steel off a striker onto char — the method that worked for six hundred years and still works when the ferro rod is gone.
time: seconds, given char and a prepared bundle

steps.text: Hold a piece of char on top of the stone, pinched under your thumb, right at the striking edge.
Strike DOWN along the stone's edge with the steel at a shallow angle, as though shaving a curl off it.
steps.why: The spark is a shaving of steel, heated to burning by the friction of being cut off. The stone is not the thing that burns — it is the blade doing the cutting.

steps.text: Aim the shower so it lands ON the char, not near it.
When the char catches, a red ring spreads across it. Fold it into the tinder bundle and blow steadily.
If the sparks are weak, freshen the stone edge by knocking a flake off — a rounded edge stops cutting steel.

verify: Orange sparks that ARC rather than flash, and a red ring that spreads across the char once one lands.
Stainless steel will not work. If you get nothing at all, the striker is the suspect before the stone is.
limits: It cannot ignite raw tinder. Without char (or true amadou) this method does essentially nothing, which is why `fire-char-cloth` is its prerequisite rather than an accessory.
It is far slower and fussier than a ferro rod. Its virtue is that both halves are findable or forgeable and never run out.
cautions: Stainless steel and modern knife steels are the usual reason this fails — you need HIGH CARBON steel, which is why an old file is the classic striker.
Struck stone throws sharp flakes. Mind your eyes and the hand holding the char.
